references.text: The parallel account in Numbers where the Lord commands Moses to send spies into the land of Canaan. Both texts describe the sending of men to explore the land.
Moses gives the spies instructions to investigate the land, its cities, and its people—this corresponds with the people's request to know about the route and the cities they are to enter.
The description of the spies' actual exploration of the land, which resulted from the request mentioned in Deuteronomy 1:22.
Joshua sends spies to Jericho to explore the land, an action similar to what the people requested in Deuteronomy 1:22.
A recollection of when the fathers were sent from Kadesh-Barnea to see the land, referring to the same event.
The immediate continuation where Moses approves the plan and selects twelve men, one from each tribe, to spy out the land.
